bib.title: Towards Language Models That Can See: Computer Vision Through the LENS of Natural Language

question: Can a frozen off-the-shelf LLM solve object recognition and vision-and-language tasks from text produced by independent vision modules, with no multimodal pretraining?
hypothesis: Rich textual descriptions (tags, attributes, captions) from pretrained vision modules let a frozen LLM match multimodally pretrained systems without any alignment training.
contributions: We propose LENS, a modular approach that addresses computer vision tasks by harnessing the few-shot, in-context learning abilities of language models through natural language descriptions of visual inputs.
LENS enables any off-the-shelf LLM to have visual capabilities without requiring auxiliary training or data.
Zero-shot performance competitive with or superior to end-to-end jointly pre-trained models like Kosmos and Flamingo.

method.summary: An image is converted to text by three frozen vision modules (CLIP-based tag module, CLIP-based attribute module, BLIP intensive captioner); the text is concatenated with a task question and fed to a frozen Flan-T5 which generates a short answer. Nothing is trained; evaluation is zero-shot (plus 1- and 3-shot for object recognition).

limits: Vision ability is bounded by CLIP and BLIP; failure cases are incorrect visual information, inconsistency across turns, presuppositions and forgetting (Fig 5).
Evaluation still needs substantial compute (8 A100), though less than Flamingo training.
Few-shot gave no improvement on V&L tasks so only zero-shot is reported; object recognition gain over CLIP is under one point.
Task-specific module selection (e.g. captioning only for VQA) was chosen from preliminary experiments, so the per-task configuration is tuned.
Baseline numbers are copied from other papers; no seeds or variance; Table 7 and Table 3 disagree.
Sec 4.1 says OK-VQA test and Rendered SST2 evaluated, Table 6 lists validation splits.
Compared systems (2023) are dated; LENS does not exceed BLIP-2 on VQAv2 or OK-VQA.
